hypotheses.text: Core neurodevelopmental features such as speech and language delay maintain high penetrance (>90%) across both the discovery series (Stolerman et al., 2019) and expanded international cohorts (Rots et al., 2023), showing no statistically significant phenotypic dilution (Fisher's exact test p > 0.05).
hypotheses.rationale: Initial disease gene discovery cohorts often suffer from ascertainment bias towards severe presentations. Demonstrating that speech and language impairment remains near-ubiquitous in expanded cohorts confirms it as an essential diagnostic criterion for KDM6B-related disorder rather than an artifact of recruitment.

evidence.text: Stolerman et al. (2019) initially reported de novo KDM6B alterations in a discovery cohort of 12 unrelated patients presenting consistently with developmental delay, intellectual disability, and dysmorphic facial features.

(2023) cohort (evaluating n=72 individuals).
hypotheses.rationale: Quantifying the exact shift in gastrointestinal phenotype prevalence clarifies whether feeding and GI manifestations represent primary manifestations of KDM6B chromatin disruption or secondary complications of severe hypotonia and general syndromic ascertainment.

evidence.text: Rots et al. assembled 73 individuals with KDM6B variants to refine the phenotypic spectrum, noting that dysmorphic and non-neurological features varied considerably across the broader cohort compared to initially defined classic phenotypes.

hypotheses.text: Craniofacial dysmorphism in KDM6B-related disorder is non-pathognomonic and exhibits lower penetrance in expanded cohorts than the 100% frequency originally observed in discovery cohorts, demonstrating that recognizable facial gestalt cannot independently exclude or confirm Stolerman syndrome.
hypotheses.rationale: If facial dysmorphism drops significantly below 100% in unselected, exome-first cohorts, clinicians cannot rely on facial gestalts to rule out Stolerman syndrome, reinforcing the primacy of unbiased genomic testing over dysmorphology matching.

evidence.text: Literature review and case reports of KDM6B-related disorder classify the condition as having non-pathognomonic facial and body dysmorphisms alongside wide neurodevelopmental and behavioral heterogeneity.

evidence.text: Recent genetic screens demonstrate wide differences in the entire phenotypic spectrum among patients with KDM6B variants, including diverse and variable facial characteristics rather than a uniform syndromic facies.
